Accroches écrites : « Things that make you quietly confident » (retenue : le gabarit exact, la confiance parle plus au public que le raffinement), « Habits that make you quietly attractive » (écartée : trop proche de talking-women déjà déposé), « Things that make you quietly sophisticated » (écartée : copie du gagnant). slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you
quietly confident
Walk slower. Not lazy, just unhurried. People who rush everywhere look like they're late for someone else's plan. Slow down on the street, in the office, through a doorway. It reads as calm.
Stop over-explaining. "I can't make it Friday." Full stop. No list of reasons, no apology essay. The more you justify a simple no, the more it sounds like you're asking for permission.
Let people finish their sentences, even when you know where they're going. Wait a beat after they stop, then answer. Interrupting looks eager. Waiting looks like you have nothing to prove.
Keep learning things nobody asked you to. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. You won't show it off, but when a topic comes up, you'll actually know what you're talking about.
slides.texte_sophia: Keep learning things nobody asked you to. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. When a topic comes up, you'll actually know your stuff.

slides.texte_overlay: Say "I don't know" without flinching. "No idea, actually. How does it work?" Pretending to know everything is what insecure people do. Admitting it calmly makes everything else you say more believable.
Dress one notch above the room. Not a suit at a barbecue. Just a clean shirt that fits and shoes that aren't falling apart. You'll never feel underdressed, and that alone changes how you stand.
Don't announce your plans. Start the gym, the side project, the language. Tell people once it's already working. "Oh, I've been doing it for six months." Quiet results hit harder than loud promises.
